stories.title: Watch Mode - Continuous File Monitoring
stories.content: Developer runs `memo` or `memo watch` to continuously monitor file changes. The flow: main.go calls cmd.Execute() which dispatches to watchCmd (default). runWatch() validates MOONSHOT_API_KEY exists, starts background update check via internal.CheckUpdateAsync(), loads config.yaml and merges .gitignore patterns. It acquires an exclusive lock via analyzer.TryLock(), creates .memo/index/*.json if missing, then creates Analyser and Watcher. Unless --skip-scan is set, it calls watcher.ScanAll() for initial full scan. PrintBanner() displays ASCII art, version, and update notice. watcher.Run(ctx) starts the fsnotify event loop. On file changes, debounce timer starts; after debounce (or maxWait), the semaphore guard ensures one analysis at a time, then calls onChange(files). Analyser.Analyse() batches files, sends to Kimi API, validates JSON output (retry up to 5x), and writes updated index files. Loop continues until Ctrl+C.

stories.title: Scan Mode - One-Shot Analysis
stories.content: Developer runs `memo scan` to analyze all files once and exit. Useful for CI or initial setup. The flow: cmd.Execute() dispatches to scanCmd. runScan() validates API key, loads config, acquires lock, initializes index. Creates Analyser and Watcher, calls watcher.ScanAll() to queue all files, then watcher.Flush() blocks until analysis completes. Releases lock and exits with status 0. This replaces the old --once flag with an explicit subcommand.

stories.title: MCP Mode - AI Agent Queries Index
stories.content: AI agent uses MCP protocol to query .memo/index for codebase context. Agent spawns `memo mcp -p /path/to/project`. cmd/mcp.go validates .memo/index exists (must run watch/scan first). mcp/server.go creates Server and starts JSON-RPC loop over stdio. Agent sends initialize request, server responds with capabilities. Agent can call memo_list_keys to explore structure (returns keys for objects, length for arrays) or memo_get_value to retrieve specific values. Path format uses bracket notation like [arch][modules][0]. Server adds warning if status.json shows analysis in progress (data may be stale).

stories.title: Configuration and Gitignore Handling
stories.content: Users configure memo via config.yaml with log level, optional agent credentials, and watch settings. The watch.ignore_patterns list specifies files/directories to ignore (defaults: .git, node_modules, .memo, *.log). If a .gitignore file exists in the watched directory, MergeGitignore() parses it and adds unique patterns to ignore list. This ensures memo respects the project's existing gitignore rules without manual configuration.

stories.title: AI Analysis with Validation Loop
stories.content: When onChange callback fires, Analyser.Analyse() is called with changed files. It sets status to 'analyzing', converts absolute paths to relative (saves tokens), batches files if count exceeds threshold (default 100). Each batch creates a kimi-agent-sdk session with local MCP config (.memo/mcp.json to prevent recursion) and deterministic session ID (hash of workDir). The prompt is built from embedded templates. runPrompt() sends prompt and processes streamed response using LineBuffer (500ms timeout). After AI completes, ValidateIndex() checks JSON against schemas. If invalid, error feedback is appended and retried (max 5 times). Finally, status is set to 'idle'.

stories.title: Concurrent Analysis Guard
stories.content: The Watcher uses a capacity-1 channel (sem chan struct{}) as a binary semaphore to prevent overlapping analyses. When Flush() is called (by timer or directly), it attempts non-blocking acquisition via select with default case. If the semaphore is held (analysis running), Flush returns immediately - files remain in pending set for next timer. If acquired, it stops both debounce and max-wait timers, collects pending files, clears the set, and calls onChange. The semaphore is released via defer after callback completes.

stories.title: History Logging for Debugging
stories.content: Both MCP server and watcher write structured logs to .memo/.history as JSONL. internal.HistoryLogger provides NewHistoryLogger(memoDir, source) which creates a logger with auto-incrementing sequence numbers. MCP server logs requests/responses with duration. Watcher logs via internal.Log* functions which also write to historyLog if initialized. This dual-logging provides both real-time visibility and persistent debug logs without cluttering stdout.
